Content:
Suppose we want to plot the graph of [MATH: y=\sin x,] where [MATH: x] is measured in radians.

Content:
First, let's create a table of values and include some of the values that we know:

Content:
| [MATH: x] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: \dfrac\pi 4] | [MATH: \dfrac\pi 2] | [MATH: \dfrac{3\pi} 4] | [MATH: \pi] | [MATH: \dfrac{5\pi} 4] | [MATH: \dfrac{3\pi} 2] | [MATH: \dfrac{7\pi} 4] | [MATH: 2\pi] |
| [MATH: \sin x] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: \dfrac{\sqrt 2}{2}] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: \dfrac{\sqrt 2}{2}] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: -\dfrac{\sqrt 2}{2}] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: -\dfrac{\sqrt 2}{2}] | [MATH: 0] |

Content:
Plotting these points, we get the following curve.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/ed8f095c1c70f61418d4825a37bb7799]

Content:
From the unit circle, we know that the function [MATH: y=\sin x] repeats itself every [MATH: 2\pi] radians. So we can extend our plot using this periodicity property.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/27994b3eb07fe894b7c661201b3b1c12]

Content:
The key characteristics of the graph are:

Content:
- The domain of the function is [MATH: x\in(-\infty,\infty).]
- The range of the function is [MATH: y\in[-1,1].]
- The period of the function is [MATH: 2\pi.]
- Its zeros occur at [MATH: x=0, \pm \pi, \pm 2\pi,\ldots.]
- Its maximum values occur at [MATH: \ldots,-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ldots]
- Its minimum values occur at [MATH: \ldots,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2},\ldots]

sections.normalized_html:
Let's recall some of the basic properties of [MATH: y=\sin{x}\mathbin{:}]

  • The minimum value is [MATH: -1,] and the maximum value is [MATH: 1.]

  • The period of the function is [MATH: 2\pi.]

  • Its zeros occur at [MATH: x=0, \pm \pi, \pm 2\pi,\ldots.]

  • Its maximum values occur at [MATH: \ldots,-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ldots]

  • Its minimum values occur at [MATH: \ldots,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2},\ldots]

Of the given plots, the only one that displays all of these properties is I.
